subject: Prompt spend scenarios + mop-up asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@paylytics.com>, PayLytics Procurement <procurement@paylytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt spend scenarios + mop-up asks

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a single source-of-truth and a set of concrete next steps.

High-level summary (what we heard)
- Primary pain: token spend and tail latency when batch windows are tightened — engineering is seeing inconsistent per-token cost across flows.
- Goal: run a 6-week pilot to validate latency (95p < 300ms) for customer-facing flows and test unit economics at scale; target pilot budget cap: $8k/month.
- Usage profile you shared: ~200k requests/month, ~80 tokens/request average, mix of short prompts (system+user ~70%) and longer completion bursts (30%).

Cost/TCO levers we discussed
- Model variant: recommend trying the 1.7B quantized variant for chat-heavy, lower-latency traffic (expected ~30–45% token-cost reduction vs baseline 7B).
- Batching/windowing: 20–40ms dynamic batching window with request prioritization for interactive flows; we expect 10–18% cost reduction while preserving latency SLOs.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching for the top 15 intents (estimated 6–12% effective token savings).
- Fallback policy: route non-critical bulk inference to cheaper capacity tier during peak to protect latency for the interactive lane.

Estimate snapshot (very rough, see attached TCO sheet for calc)
- Baseline monthly token estimate: 200k * 80 = 16M tokens
- Ballpark hosted cost (after batching/caching mix above): ~$6.5k–$8k/month (aligned with your $8k cap if we start conservative and tune).

Attachments: paylytics_tco_sheet.xlsx (breakdown by model/quantization/batching scenarios)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm procurement timeline and whether PayLytics needs SOC2 + SSO + IP addendum up front? (Procurement pinged on call)
2) Please confirm the two pilot owner names (engineering + project sponsor) so we can send a 6-week SOW draft.
3) If the usage numbers above are off, share actual monthly request counts or a short sample CSV and I’ll re-run the calc.

Proposed quick cadence
- This week: exchange SOW + TCO sheet (I’ll attach drafts).
- Next week: 30-min pilot kickoff with engineering to agree on routes to instrument and latency checks.

If helpful I can also run an alternate scenario with a more aggressive 50ms batching window vs 20ms to show sensitivity.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: paylytics_tco_sheet.xlsx (xlsx, 84 KB)]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@paylytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: PayLytics Procurement <procurement@paylytics.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt spend scenarios + mop-up asks

Thanks Jonas — helpful recap and good alignment. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Procurement needs: SOC 2 type II report + standard SSO (Okta) + default data residency in us-west. They also asked whether Redwood offers a standard IP/data addendum or if we need legal redlines.
- Usage refinement: the 200k requests is an average month — expected ramp in Q4 could push to ~350k, but pilot should focus on the 200k baseline. Average tokens ~80 is correct, but interactive flows skew shorter (~40 tokens) and the longer batch completions push the average.
- Success criteria: 1) 95p latency under 300ms for interactive routes, 2) demonstrable >20% reduction in effective token spend vs our existing endpoint after pilot tuning.

Procurement asked if you can share a one-page TCO summary for stakeholders (cost buckets and assumptions) and a draft SOW they can circulate. Also: is there a sandbox for us to run sample traces or do you prefer we share a sample CSV for you to simulate?

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product 
PayLytics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@paylytics.com>, PayLytics Procurement <procurement@paylytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt spend scenarios + mop-up asks

Elena — appreciate the clarifications. Quick replies inline and next artifacts attached.

- Procurement: we can provide SOC 2 type II report and support Okta SSO. I’ve attached a short one-page TCO summary that explicitly lists assumptions (see paylytics_tco_sheet.xlsx). For legal, we have a standard MSA/SOW + a one-page data addendum; if PayLytics has redlines we can ingest them into our standard doc.
- Sandbox / sample traces: we don’t spin up a dedicated sandbox for pilot sims, but if you share a sample CSV with request counts and typical prompt lengths we’ll run a sensitivity simulation and return a short appendix (we can also instrument a lightweight test on hosted capacity if you want live traces).
- Ramp scenario: attached is a pair of scenarios (baseline 200k, ramp 350k) and an inline sensitivity table showing how cost-per-token moves with batching window and quantization. Under the conservative mix we arrive at ~$7.2k for 200k and ~$11.8k for 350k — the ramp puts you above your $8k cap so we’ll need to lock levers (e.g., more aggressive quantization or a burst-cap on expensive routes).

Attachments: redwood_pilot_sow_draft.pdf, paylytics_tco_sheet.xlsx (see tab: summary + sensitivity)

Action items I’ll own
- Update one-page TCO with explicit assumptions for procurement (today).
- Produce a draft 6-week SOW and send for review (tomorrow).

Action items for PayLytics
- Send sample CSV (2–3 days) OR confirm you want us to run a live trace (we’ll need an engineering contact + temporary credentials).
- Confirm primary sponsor (procurement owner + engineering owner) so we can finalize SOW signing route.

Proposed kickoff slots (PT): Thu 08/27 10:00–10:30, Thu 08/27 15:00–15:30 — pick one and I’ll calendar-in.

Thanks — Jonas
[Attachments: redwood_pilot_sow_draft.pdf (pdf, 32 KB); paylytics_tco_sheet.xlsx (xlsx, 84 KB)]

Looping in a quick ops note from our side:
- Region: us-west is fine for initial pilot; we’ll gate data residency in the SOW.
- GPU profile: start on a mixed pool with A100s for bulk processing and A10s for interactive lanes — ops can size once we have a sampled CSV.
- Can someone confirm if PayLytics expects dedicated capacity for the pilot or if hosted (shared) with an agreed SLA is sufficient? That changes the pricing materially; procurement usually flags dedicated as a later ask.

I’ll stand by to provision whoever you name as engineering owner.

—Marissa
